critic: LEAD (independent critic, checked by a second agent)
verdict:
C20: evidence_table at 64abcff, judged on the screen camera. The display can take a pin, and HEAD already pins it. The weak part is the laptop body around it. The stage is not at pro level, and the scores stay at the r7 values.

What I reviewed:
- screen.png, screen.jpg (2560x1440) and screen.corners.json, committed in 64abcff at 10:30.
- HEAD is 65794a9. Since 64abcff, two commits change evidence_table.py: 3afdf40 and e22216f. They touch only the plate-optics metadata and the pair/plate beat. Nothing in laptop() or the screen camera changed, so this render matches the current code.
- 65794a9 also adds the screen UI and its comp: gfx/screen.html, shots/screen_email.json, shots/screen_search.json and the texture path in doc_composite.py. I pulled frames from out/gfx/screen_email.mp4 and screen_search.mp4, because the comp decides which plate problems will actually be seen.
- I measured on the raw PNG with numpy:
  - 140 bilinear profiles across each panel edge
  - a halfway crossing on each profile
  - a line fitted to each edge, with corners where the lines meet.
- The other seven frames are the files r7 saw:
  - page.jpg (75c2212, 09:21) still has the khaki marker.
  - pair.jpg (f720f32, 09:56) predates e22216f's spot, lamp and contact-edge changes.
  - overhead, push, laptop, purses and passport are the 04:54 renders (7249565).
- So the stage scores do not move.

The display:
- Even, neutral and clean.
  - Raw panel luma is 192.4 with std 1.1 and range 189-194. It falls about 2.6 levels from top to bottom.
  - Colour is RGB 189/193/197, and high-pass noise std is about 0.4-0.5.
  - The graded panel runs about 138-187 (1st-99th percentile) and is darkest in the corners. That is the grade's vignette, not the panel.
- The four corners are square and sharp, and the gasket does not overlap the panel.
- The black surround is clean: raw medians 4-8, p95 6-12, with no fireflies or blotches.
  - 26% of graded pixels are below luma 8. For a night insert that is acceptable, because the wood still reads at the bottom corners (graded 13-18).
- The blotchy band r7 found on the left bezel is gone.

What fights the pinned screen now is not the keys but the generated laptop body:

(1) A crumpled, wavy glossy band runs across the hinge directly under the panel.
- It is about 1,300 px wide at raw y 1085-1160, with raw p95 131 and max 151.
- It and the palm rest are the brightest things after the panel.
- It looks like the panel mirrored in lumpy generated geometry, and it reads as cling film.
- It shows in the email comp. At the start it lies across the bottom of the frame (output p95 about 90-100). When the push lands, it sits on the frame's bottom edge (output p95 85 in the last 40 rows).

(2) The palm rest along the plate's bottom edge is a bright glossy band: raw p95 148, graded 111.
- In an uncropped plate it would pull the eye out of the bottom of the frame.
- Both HEAD shots crop it out. The email crop ends at plate y 1241 at the start and about 1127 at the end, and the search crop ends at about 929.
- So it matters only if the plate is ever cut uncropped.

(3) Three faint letter-like marks remain:
- a dotted strip, like an embossed wordmark or a vent, at the right end of the hinge band (raw x about 1750-1900, y 1100-1120), up to about raw 105
- a short dashed mark centred on the lid chin under the panel, like a badge (raw x 1265-1350, y about 1025). It is faint: it peaks at raw 17 on a chin of 10 (graded 22 on 15).
- pale specks between the keys of the upper rows, peaking at about raw 80-85 on keys around 45.

(4) The screen shows no reflection.
- The HEAD comp multiplies the UI into the plate's own glow in linear light. The UI therefore carries the panel's falloff and the grade, and it already reads as a lit screen, not a sticker.
- A reflection pass would be polish, and in a room this dark it may hold almost nothing.

Composition:
- The plate is a centred, frontal, static framing with about 85 px of headroom over the lid.
- The comps crop into it with a log-space push: email zoom 1.16-1.26 on the message, search 1.55-1.65. So the plate's own framing matters less than what sits at the bottom of the email crop, which is the hinge band.
- In script v2 this camera serves chapter 01 (the email and the search, before the passport details and the tickets). The screen carries the story there, so nothing else needs to be in frame.

Craft bar:
- Next to the koi-pond stills, the keyboard is acceptable as a soft foreground.
- The hinge and palm rest look like an unretouched generated mesh.
answers:
1. The four corners.

I measured the visible panel corners on the raw 2560x1440 PNG:
- 140 bilinear profiles across each edge
- the halfway crossing between panel (12-22 px in) and bezel (12-22 px out)
- a line fitted to each edge: RMS 0.06-0.08 px, max 0.22 px.

On gamma-encoded luma, as you measured:

| Corner | Visible corner (px) | JSON pin (px) | Distance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top left | 648.36, 104.85 | 648.79, 105.23 | 0.58 px |
| Top right | 1916.69, 101.09 | 1916.03, 101.72 | 0.92 px |
| Bottom right | 1947.40, 953.01 | 1947.01, 952.67 | 0.51 px |
| Bottom left | 655.30, 980.91 | 656.03, 980.21 | 1.01 px |

- Your 0.53-1.06 px is confirmed: I get 0.51-1.05 px.
- Every edge sits outside its pinned line, and evenly: top +0.52, right +0.54, bottom +0.53, left +0.6 px.
- In linear light the corners are 0.23-0.50 px off and the edges +0.24 to +0.30 px out. Most of the offset is gamma bias.
- The pins are good.

For the comp:
- doc_composite.py already warps the texture through a full homography (getPerspectiveTransform from the four pins). Keep it, because the lid is yawed (corner depths 0.763-0.800 m):
  - The bottom edge rises 27.5 px from left to right (980.2 at the left, 952.7 at the right).
  - The top edge rises only 3.5 px (105.2 at the left, 101.7 at the right).
- The edges are near-sharp everywhere. Focus is 0.781 m at f/2.2, and the corners spread 36 mm in depth.
  - The 10-90% edge width is 1.3-1.5 px at the top-left and bottom-right.
  - It is 1.9-2.1 px at the top-right (farthest) and bottom-left (nearest).
  - One warp with the comp's uniform 0.55 px softening is fine.
- The HEAD UI already has light edges (#eceef1 bars, #f4f5f7 and #ffffff fields), and the comp multiplies it into the glow. So the 0.5 px sliver of blank glow outside the pins cannot be seen. Expand the quad by about 0.3 px only if a dark UI is ever pinned.

2. The black surround and the bezel.

The surround is clean for compositing: raw medians 4-8, p95 6-12, and no fireflies, blotches or denoiser smears.

The bezel ring is quiet (raw luma):

| Outside the pinned edge | Median | p95 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2-14 px | 9-12 | 11-13 |
| 14-24 px | 10-24 | 31-43, max 57 |

- The 14-24 px band holds a thin grey hairline on all four sides. It peaks 19-22 px out, about 4-5 mm at this distance.
- The hairline is 3-4x the bezel median, so the 1.3x target from r7 fails.
- It is most likely the lid's raised lip catching the panel's glow, not the edge of the 'LCD inner bezel' box.
  - The liner's front face sits about 1.7 mm proud of the lid plane.
  - The lip is more than 2.5 mm proud from 3 mm outside the panel.
  - So the liner's outer edge is buried under the lip.
- It reads as a plausible bezel edge, so it is a minor, optional fix (fix 5). It does show in the email comp as a second frame line.
- The blotchy left band from r7 is gone: the left 14-24 px band median is 11.

3. Keyboard.

The fall in key p95 is confirmed:
- Over raw y 1160-1400, x 520-2150, graded p95 is 50.8 (raw 55.5) and the graded median is 30.
- The key tops are dark and matte.

The bright things on the laptop are now elsewhere:
- the hinge strip: raw p95 131, max 151, graded p95 110
- the palm rest along the plate's bottom edge: raw p95 148, graded 111
- faint pale specks between the keys of the upper rows: they peak at about raw 80-85 on keys around 45 (38 pixels stand more than 15 levels above their local median).
  - The 1155-1185 band's p99 of about 146 comes from the hinge highlight's lower edge, not from the specks.

The hinge strip and the palm rest are the two brightest things after the panel. Both look like glossy mirrors of the panel on bumpy generated geometry.

4. Does the display hold attention through the cut?

Yes:
- In the plate, the panel is about 30% of the frame at raw 192.
- Outside it, only the hinge smear and the palm glare go above about 70 (both up to 150).
- The HEAD comps make it hold more firmly:
  - The email shot frames the screen at about 60% of the width and 70% of the height, with a push onto the message.
  - The search shot is almost all screen.
  - The palm rest never appears in either shot.

What still competes is the hinge smear in the email shot:
- At the start it runs across the bottom of the frame at output p95 about 90-100.
- When the push lands, it sits on the bottom frame edge, where the eye leaves the screen.

Removing it (fix 1) is what makes the 7.5 s email shot hold cleanly. The push and the durations are already in the shot files.

Two more checks:
- Nothing in the plate breaks the no-text rule outright.
- The hinge's dotted strip, the faint chin badge and the key specks are letter-like and should go.

fixes.problem:
A crumpled, wavy glossy band runs across the hinge directly under the panel:
- It is about 1,300 px wide at raw y 1085-1160.
- Raw p95 is 131 and max 151; graded p95 is 110.
- It looks like the panel mirrored in the generated laptop's lumpy hinge and deck-back surface, and it reads as cling film.
- It carries the letter-like dotted strip at raw x about 1750-1900, y 1100-1120.
- It is the one plate flaw inside the HEAD email comp. It crosses the bottom of the frame at the start (output p95 about 90-100) and sits on the bottom frame edge when the push lands.
fixes.fix:
In laptop(), after the 'laptop key well' box, cover the strip between the key well and the lid with flat matte geometry:
1. Add a bevelled box, sk.box('laptop hinge cover', ...):
   - It runs from the key well's back edge (x = -0.009 + 0.066 = 0.057 in prop space) to xs(zbot) - 0.002. Compute the depth from those two values rather than hard-coding it.
   - Make it 0.325 wide and 0.004 thick, with its top at z 0.0262. Raise the top if the generated surface still shows through.
   - Use mt.plastic('keyboard surround', (0.019, 0.021, 0.023), 0.65, spec=0.24) and bevel 0.0015.
2. Optionally add a hinge barrel in the same material: sk.cyl, radius 0.0055, length 0.30, rotated so its axis runs along Y, at the lid's foot.
3. Add the new objects to the placement loop `for o in (scr, li, fx, deck, keys, liner)` and to the returned list, so they move and hide with the laptop.
4. Re-render screen at 2560x1440.
5. Target on the raw frame: in y 1085-1160, x 620-1950, p95 is 60 or less, with no wavy highlight and no dotted strip.
6. Re-run the email comp and check its bottom 140 rows.

fixes.problem:
The palm rest along the plate's bottom edge is a bright glossy band:
- In raw y 1370-1440, p95 is 148 (graded 111) and max 154.
- It is most likely the panel's mirror image in the generated body. Even with roughness raised by 0.12, the body is too glossy.
- In an uncropped plate it is the brightest thing on a frame edge, and it pulls the eye out of the bottom.
- Both HEAD shots crop it out: the email crop ends at plate y 1241-1127 and the search crop at about 929. So this matters only if the plate is ever cut uncropped.
fixes.fix:
Raise the laptop body's roughness in one of two ways:
- Change props.load('laptop', ..., rough_add=0.12) to rough_add=0.45. This also changes the `laptop` camera, so check that frame too.
- Or, for the screen camera only, in apply_camera() add 0.3 to Roughness on every material under the laptop holder (G['laptop'][0].children_recursive).

If the band is still above target, extend the matte key well forward over the palm rest:
- depth 0.132 to 0.20
- centre x -0.009 to -0.043, which keeps the back edge at 0.057.

Target: raw p95 of 80 or less in y 1370-1440. Keep a soft sheen there, not a hard band.

fixes.problem:
Two more faint letter-like marks remain. Anything letter-like should go.
1. A short dashed mark centred on the lid chin under the panel, like a model badge:
   - It is at raw x 1265-1350, y about 1025.
   - It is faint: peak raw 17 on a chin of 10 (graded 22 on 15).
   - The brighter tab just above it (raw y 981-990, max about 41) is the lid's lip, not lettering.
2. Pale specks between the keys of the upper rows:
   - They peak at about raw 80-85 on keys around 45 (38 pixels stand more than 15 levels above their 15 px local median, in y 1165-1250).
   - They are probably the generated deck's pale keycap shapes showing through the 2.3 mm gaps between the blank keys.
fixes.fix:
1. Chin: add sk.box('lid chin cover', (w + 0.011, 0.018, 0.0003), ...) in the 'LCD bezel' gasket material.
   - Use the liner's rot and centre it at centre - up * (hh/2 + 0.014).
   - Do not place it at the liner's depth. The chin stands more than 2.5 mm proud of the lid plane, while the liner's face is only about 1.7 mm proud, so a cover at the liner's depth would be buried. Set its offset along nrm to the largest dev() over that chin band plus 0.0003.
   - Add it to the 'screen spill' group and to the placement loop.
   - Target: the mark is no more than 3 levels above the chin median.
2. Specks: raise 'laptop key well' to centre z 0.0250 with thickness 0.0040, so its top is at 0.0270.
   - Raise the key boxes in add_box from z 0.026 to 0.0285.
   - Target: in raw y 1165-1250, x 700-1900, no pixel stands more than 15 levels above its 15 px local median.

fixes.problem:
The plate has no reflection layer:
- The HEAD comp multiplies the UI into the plate's glow in linear light, so it already takes the panel's falloff and the grade.
- In the email and search comps it reads as a lit screen.
- What it lacks is any reflection, which in a room this dark would be faint anyway.

There is also no screen matte:
- install_hook() writes a matte only for page, page_foot and pair, and only for outputs named final*.
- laptop_screen has no pass_index.
- A matte is not needed here: the panel is flat and unoccluded, and its pins are within about 1 px.
fixes.fix:
Optional polish. Test before committing to it:
1. Render a reflection pass, screen.glass.png:
   - Set the 'laptop screen' material's emission strength to 0.
   - Give the panel a near-black base (0.005), roughness 0.18 and specular IOR level 0.5.
   - Keep the lamp at its ch02 level (0.25) and render only the panel, with holdout elsewhere.
2. Use it only if it holds visible structure, such as the lamp head or the lit table. If it does, the comp screens it over the pinned UI at about 0.3-0.5.
3. If it comes back near black, drop it. The multiply comp is enough.

fixes.problem:
A thin grey hairline rings the bezel:
- It peaks 19-22 px outside the panel edge, about 4-5 mm at this distance.
- In the 14-24 px band it reaches p95 31-43 and max 57, against a bezel median of 9-12. It shows in the email comp as a second frame line around the screen.
- It is most likely the lid's raised lip catching the panel's glow, not the edge of the 'LCD inner bezel' box:
  - laptop() insets the panel 3 mm inside the point where the lid stands 2.5 mm proud.
  - The render log gives 1.2 mm proud for the recess, so the liner's front face sits about 1.7 mm proud, and its outer 2-2.5 mm already runs under the lip.
  - Widening the liner would only slide more of it under the lip.
- It reads as a plausible bezel edge, so this fix is optional.
fixes.fix:
If the hairline is to go:
1. Lay a thin matte frame on top of the lip in the 'LCD bezel' material: four sk.box strips, 0.3 mm thick, covering 2.5-7 mm outside each panel edge.
   - Use the liner's rot. Offset each strip along nrm to the largest dev() in its band plus 0.0003.
   - Add the strips to 'screen spill' and to the placement loop.
2. Alternatively, apply the roughness raise from the palm-rest fix first and re-measure.
3. Target: in the 14-24 px band outside the pins, p95 is no more than 1.3x the bezel median (about 15).

fixes.fix:
Re-render from HEAD and regrade with A fixed:
- overhead, push, laptop, purses and passport at 1280x720 or 2560x1440
- page, page_foot and pair at 2560x1440, with corners and masks.

Then check the r7 targets:
- overhead: under 5% of graded pixels below 8
- pair: document_left's (5 mm, 5 mm) point is at least 0.92 of its (30 mm, 30 mm) point
- page marker: hue 52-58 degrees and saturation 0.45 or more.

If overhead's far wood still grades under 8, add r7's warm 0.6 x 0.4 m area light at (0.35, 0.15), 1 m above the table.
